agree.reason: The direct apology, plain bad news and the ex-chain growth figure will ease a cold lead angel, but there is no commitment to regular updates, no fundraising plan and no target for the reminder launch, so this reader has little to judge future backing against.

honest.reason: The figures check out ($35,500 to $41,000 is about 15%, 13% to 7% is close to half, $480k / $44k is about 11 months), but 'net +5 clinics' hides that the lost chain was 12 clinic locations, and calling EHR schedulers 'the biggest competitive threat' goes further than the facts given.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the runway, the growth excluding the chain and the size of the no-show cut, all in favourable true forms, but it doesn't work out what the reminder product or the core growth rate would need to reach to extend runway or break even.

right_comparison.reason: It contrasts standalone reminders with trying to win customers away from built-in schedulers, but never shows what happens if nothing changes: at about 15% quarterly growth outside the chain, the cash still runs out around late 2027.

qualification.reason: The only hedge, 'the main thing I'll be watching', gives no sales target, no date and no consequence if the launch falls short, even though there are just 11 months of runway.

objections.reason: It deals with the missed updates and the churn to EHR schedulers, but leaves out this reader's main concerns: when the next round is, how it will be raised with 11 months of cash, and whether updates will now arrive every quarter.

fit.reason: It is a clear, scannable investor update of roughly 430 words, under the limit and in a format that suits 11 investors.
